text: Genome and phenome analysis of 157 industrial *Saccharomyces cerevisiae* strains shows they form five sublineages, genetically and phenotypically distinct from wild strains, descending from few ancestors through complex domestication and local divergence. Large-scale phenotyping reveals industry-specific selection for stress tolerance, sugar utilization, and flavor production, while sexual cycle and nature-survival traits decay, notably in beer yeasts. Separately, ribosomal protein gene *RPL32* is essential, encoding a 105-amino-acid protein (basic N-terminus, acidic C-terminus) homologous to mammalian L30, with a confirmed 230-nucleotide intron beginning GTCAGT. Transcription starts 58 nucleotides upstream of AUG; polyadenylation occurs 100 nucleotides downstream of the stop codon. Deleting three regulatory sequences between RP29 and RPL32 reduces L32-LacZ fusion synthesis over 90%, with residual activity. Yeast histone acetylation/deacetylation directs acetyltransferases and deacetylases to promoters, affecting most nucleosomes, with roles in DNA replication, repair, and heterochromatin formation.
